title: A generically finite morphism over a finite generic fibre is finite over a dense open of the target
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a locally finite type morphism whose generic fibres match up, in the sense that the preimages of the generic points of the target are exactly the generic points of the source, with finitely many such points, is finite over a dense open of the target, provided the morphism is quasi-compact or separated (statement lines 13328-13339). The counted proof is a two-case argument: after reducing to an irreducible affine target it applies generic finiteness and uses closedness of finite morphisms to show the open piece already exhausts the preimage in the separated case, and in the quasi-compact case it first restricts to a dense open separated subscheme of the source and then reduces to the separated case by pushing the complement away from the generic point (proof lines 13341-13367). It is H2: both cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being generic finiteness, closedness of finite morphisms and the existence of dense separated opens.
